title: What an AI agent can do on Bird: CLI, MCP, terminal signup, and spend controls
summary: What an AI agent uses on Bird, with links: the bird CLI, the hosted MCP server, account signup from a terminal, and the controls on what it can spend.
body_markdown:
In September we announced that[Bird's communications infrastructure is open to AI agents](https://bird.com/blog/bird-450-million-financing-agentic-harness) . This post is the developer's version of that announcement. It names the commands an agent runs, what it connects to, how it gets an account, and the limits you can put on it, each with the page that documents it.


## The CLI


An agent that can run shell commands, such as Claude Code, Cursor's terminal, or a CI job, should start with the CLI: it uses far fewer tokens for each operation than MCP does. The MCP server, described next, is for hosts that call tools and cannot run a shell, and for MCP Events.


` bird` is a single binary built to be driven by an agent. Output is JSON on stdout, errors go to stderr, and the exit code carries the failure category, so an agent can branch on the result without parsing prose.


```text
curl   -fsSL   https://cli.bird.com/install.sh   |   sh
bird   auth   login
```


Three flags do most of the work for an agent.` --example` prints a valid request body,` --dry-run` shows the request without sending it, and` --idempotency-key` makes a retry safe when a response is lost.[CLI for agents](https://bird.com/docs/ai/cli-for-agents) describes the contract, and the[CLI reference](https://bird.com/docs/cli) lists each command.


## The hosted MCP server


Some hosts call tools and cannot run a shell, such as Claude Desktop, ChatGPT, or a mobile app. For those, the Bird MCP server runs at` https://mcp.bird.com` . Give that URL to an MCP client and sign in through your browser, and the client holds a token that acts as you. The consent screen shows the permissions the client asks for, and you can clear the ones the agent does not need. You install nothing and copy no API key. Supported clients include Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Codex, Claude, ChatGPT, and Muse, and Bird is listed in[Claude's connector directory](https://claude.ai/directory/bird) .


The server exposes the Bird API as tools, so a connected agent can send on the channels Bird runs, set those channels up, and inspect your workspace. A client with a limit on the number of tools can connect to` https://mcp.bird.com/dynamic` , which lists two tools:` search` finds an operation and` execute` calls it. With[MCP Events](https://bird.com/docs/ai/mcp-events) , a client subscribes to what happens in your workspace, such as an inbound SMS or new mail in a mailbox, so the agent does not poll for it.


[MCP server](https://bird.com/docs/ai/mcp-server) has the steps for each client. Once the CLI is installed,` bird mcp` runs a local server over stdio. It adds the signup tools and uploads from local files, and it does not serve MCP Events.


## Signup from a terminal


An agent that has no account can create one from a terminal, with no browser session and no dashboard visit. It needs access to an email inbox, because the sign-in code arrives by email:


```text
bird   auth   signup   you@example.com
bird   auth   verify-email   you@example.com   --code   123456
bird   auth   create-org   "  Acme  "   --workspace-name   "  Production  "   --region   eu1   --onboarding-ticket   "  YOUR_ONBOARDING_TICKET  "
```


` bird auth create-org` creates the organization and its workspace, and stores a credential that the CLI and the local MCP server use from then on.` --region` chooses where the account and its data live,` us1` or` eu1` . The same three steps work with curl, for an agent that has no CLI. The hosted MCP server does not offer signup, because a client needs a credential before it can connect there.


That first credential is broad. It holds the permissions the new organization's owner can delegate, organization billing included, and signup shows no consent screen to narrow it. Before an agent runs unattended,[create a scoped API key](https://bird.com/docs/ai/agent-controls#choose-the-credential-the-agent-holds) for it.[Self-serve signup](https://bird.com/docs/ai/self-serve-signup) walks through both paths.


## Controls on what an agent can do


An agent that sends through Bird holds a credential and spends your balance.[Agent controls](https://bird.com/docs/ai/agent-controls) documents on one page what bounds it. These are the four to set before an agent runs unattended. The destination allowlist and the daily spend limit apply to SMS. Email and WhatsApp have neither, so the key's scopes and the wallet are what bound an agent there. The same page covers safe retries: send an` Idempotency-Key` header, or` --idempotency-key` on the CLI, and a repeated request is accepted once.


**Scoped API keys.** An API key belongs to one workspace and carries the scopes you give it, each a product area at` read` or` write` level. A key that sends SMS and does nothing else holds` sms:write` , and a request outside its scopes returns` 403` . A key cannot issue another key, and it cannot reach billing.


```text
bird   auth   login   --scope   api_keys:write   --scope   sms:write     # an existing account
bird   api-keys   create   --name   "  Support agent  "   --scope   sms:write
```


The sign-in must hold` api_keys:write` and the scopes the key will carry. The credential from terminal signup already holds them, so after` bird auth create-org` you run the second command alone. Do not sign in again there: a new sign-in replaces the signup credential. Run it in a shell where` BIRD_API_KEY` is not set, because the CLI uses that key in preference to a sign-in, and a key cannot issue keys.


Then give the agent the key and nothing wider. Set` BIRD_API_KEY` in the agent's environment, or send the key as a bearer token from your code. A sign-in stays stored on the machine where it ran, and an agent there with no` BIRD_API_KEY` uses it. Run the agent somewhere else, or remove the sign-in with` bird auth logout` .


**Default-deny SMS destinations.** A workspace sends SMS to the countries on its destination allowlist. The allowlist starts empty, and Bird adds your organization's home country when it is set. A send through the SMS API to any other country is rejected with` 422 SMSDestinationNotEnabled` before a sender is resolved, so an agent pointed at an unexpected country is refused. Verification codes do not use this list.[Verify](https://bird.com/docs/guides/verify/destinations) has its own, where every country starts enabled, and[Voice](https://bird.com/docs/guides/voice/destinations) has its own settings too.


**Daily spend limits.** Each SMS destination country can carry a daily spend limit, in your wallet's currency. Once the day's spend to that country reaches the limit, Bird refuses new messages there until midnight UTC. The limit is not exact: spend counts when a message is charged, so messages already accepted can take the day's total past it. Verification codes sent by SMS count toward the limit. This command enables the Netherlands with a limit of 25 EUR a day, in a workspace whose wallet is in EUR:


```text
bird   sms   destinations   update   --destination   "  NL=true;25EUR  "
```


Changing the allowlist or a limit needs the` sms_management` scope at` write` level. Give the sending agent` sms` , keep` sms_management` for the credential that configures the workspace, and the agent cannot raise its own limits.


**The prepaid wallet.** Pay-as-you-go sends draw on your organization's prepaid wallet. An SMS send that the balance cannot cover is refused with` 402` . Some charges settle after a send is accepted (email on a paid Email plan, and fees charged at delivery), and automatic top-up refills the wallet from a saved card, so read[the wallet rules](https://bird.com/docs/guides/billing-and-usage#the-wallet) before you treat the balance as a hard cap. Billing operations need the organization's billing permission, which an API key cannot hold. Give an unattended agent a scoped key, and adding funds stays with the people who own the budget.


## Where to go next


- [Give an agent its own phone number and inbox](https://bird.com/docs/ai/agent-number-and-inbox) : an` inbox.ai` address and a dedicated number that both send and receive. Before the first number, a person funds the wallet and an organization owner completes identity verification. The guide says which steps of an order need a person.
- [Bird for European customers](https://bird.com/docs/knowledge-base/compliance/european-customers) : the Dutch entity you contract with, the` eu1` region, and the Data Processing Agreement.
- [Send Supabase Auth SMS codes with Bird](https://bird.com/docs/knowledge-base/integrations/supabase) : phone sign-in codes for a Supabase project, sent through the Bird SMS API.
- [Set up your coding agent](https://bird.com/docs/ai/set-up-your-agent) : paste one prompt, and your agent installs the CLI and Bird's skills.
